q: Which is true regarding cyanotic heart disease?
o: Tetralogy of Fallot shows pulmonary plethora
Ventricular septal defect is a common cause
There is an increased risk of brain abscess
Infants are distressed in proportion to the cyanosis
e: Right-to-left shunts bypass the filter of the lungs, so brain abscess is more common.

q: Squatting with episodes of cyanosis suggests:
e: Squatting raises the systemic vascular resistance.

q: Which of the following is a cyanotic heart disease?
e: Tricuspid atresia shunts from right to left at the atrial level.

q: All of the following are associated with tetralogy of Fallot EXCEPT:
e: Tetralogy of Fallot has oligaemic lungs.

q: An 8-day-old baby becomes blue when crying. The most likely diagnosis among these is:
e: Of the options, only tetralogy of Fallot is cyanotic; severe forms present early.

q: All are associated with hypoxaemia EXCEPT:
A 4-month-old with tetralogy of Fallot becomes deeply cyanosed and breathless after crying, and the murmur is softer. What is the first step?
e: Then morphine, fluids, sodium bicarbonate and propranolol.

q: Which drug is used to prevent hypercyanotic spells?
A newborn of a diabetic mother is deeply cyanosed on day 1, with no murmur and an egg-shaped heart. What is the diagnosis?
e: Transposition of the great arteries is the commonest cyanotic congenital heart disease at birth.

q: Cyanotic heart disease with left axis deviation on the ECG suggests:
e: The right ventricle is small, so the left ventricle dominates.
